findings.title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is used after making getCalendar async. Array.forEach does not await async callbacks and returns void, so promises from await getCalendar(), calendar.deleteEvent() and deleteMeeting() are fire-and-forget. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections, and the function returns true and sends the reschedule email while deletions are still pending. Consequence: external calendar/video events are not reliably deleted, leaving orphan events and silent failures.

findings.title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is used. Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the await getCalendar() and subsequent calendar.deleteEvent()/deleteMeeting() promises are never awaited and their rejections escape the surrounding try/catch. Consequence: reschedule completes and returns true while external deletions may still be pending or have failed, leaving stale events on user calendars.

findings.title: Async forEach for reschedule cleanup is not awaited
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... }) is fire-and-forget. forEach ignores returned promises, so calendar.deleteEvent() and deleteMeeting() are not awaited before sendRequestRescheduleEmail and webhook dispatch. Consequence: previous slot may not be freed, errors are unobserved, and the mutation reports success while external cleanup failed.

findings.title: Async forEach populates apiDeletes after it is consumed
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }) runs async callbacks without awaiting them. apiDeletes is later consumed by Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)). Because pushes happen after an await, the array is still empty when it is read for recurring cancellations with allRemainingBookings. Consequence: recurring booking cancellations skip deleting external calendar events, leaving ghost events on Google/Office calendars.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in sync return value
findings.body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 28 const calendar = getCalendar(credential) now stores a Promise<Calendar|null> because getCalendar became async, but getCalendarCredentials itself stayed synchronous and still returns [{integration, credential, calendar}]. The contract changed from Calendar|null to Promise without a signature change. Any consumer not updated to await item.calendar will treat a Promise object as truthy Calendar, so checks like if (!calendar) never trigger and calls like calendar.listCalendars fail. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await; other importers break.

findings.title: Promise.all on getCalendar makes one bad integration fail all availability
findings.body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 142 const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map((credential) => getCalendar(credential))) awaits dynamic imports together. If any single import() rejects or getCalendar throws, the whole Promise.all rejects and getCachedResults throws, discarding availability for all other healthy calendars. Previously sync lookup could return null per credential. Consequence: one broken calendar app breaks availability for the entire user.

findings.title: Eager dynamic imports load all apps upfront anyway
findings.body: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the object literal evaluates import("./applecalendar"), import("./googlecalendar"), etc. immediately when the module is first imported. All 27 app chunks therefore start loading upfront just like static imports, with no on-demand lazy loading. Consequence: no cold-start or bundle-size benefit is achieved while every getCalendar/getVideoAdapter now pays an extra async tick and error-handling burden; true laziness requires functions or getters like applecalendar: () => import(...).
